q: I recorded the interview on a separate recorder. How do I get from the cards to a first cut?
a: 1. Copy each card with the card bar's verified copy (`card.offload`). 2. Line up the recorder with the camera: Merge Clips (`clip.mergeClips`, audio method) for one item per take, or Synchronize (`clip.synchronize`) on the timeline; clap at the start of every take. 3. Watch everything once and mark the usable moments: markers in the Source monitor (M), Make Subclip (`clip.makeSubclip`), a bin per scene.

q: Finish the sound of a YouTube video and export it.
a: 1. Bring the mix to about −14 LUFS with −1 dBTP peaks (Clean Up Voice matches voice clips to that; check the whole mix on the loudness meter). 2. Put a Hard Limiter insert on the Mix strip (`mixer.addInsert`) at −1 dB, after the levels are set, not to make it loud. 3. Export 4K with H.265 at constant quality (CRF) or a high bitrate, even for a 1080p audience.

q: Turn my 16:9 edit into a Short that works with the sound off.
a: 1. Duplicate the sequence (`edit.duplicate`), set it to 1080 × 1920 (`sequence.settings`) and reposition each clip with Motion ▸ Position. 2. Make captions from the transcript (`transcript.createCaptions`, short maxChars, one line), style them big with a stroke (`captions.setStyle`), burn in at export. 3. Keep text out of the bottom fifth and the right edge; check on a phone.

q: Clean up a dialogue track step by step, in the right order.
a: 1. High-pass the voice: Reduce Rumble 3–4 (66–78 Hz) or a High Pass effect. 2. Reduce noise only until the voice starts to change: Voice Isolation for changing noise, Reduce Noise for steady hiss. 3. De-ess last, after EQ and compression: DeEss 3–6 in Essential Sound.

q: Narration over a music bed: what's the order of work?
a: 1. Set the voice first: type the clips and Auto-Match them (`essentialSound.autoMatch`) or Clean Up Voice. 2. Bring the music in underneath, about 15–20 dB below the voice while words play, with Ducking (`essentialSound.generateDucking`). 3. Short crossfades at every audio edit (`sequence.applyAudioTransition`) so nothing clicks.

q: Two cameras on an interview: how do I get them ready to cut with B-roll?
a: 1. Set each camera's input space with Interpret Footage (`clip.interpretFootage`), one working space for the sequence. 2. Match the cameras, skin first, not the backgrounds. 3. Cut the interview on V1 / A1 and lay B-roll on V2, video only: target V2, source audio off (`timeline.setTargeting`), Overwrite.

q: Make a lower third I can reuse for every interviewee.
a: 1. Pin the box shape to the text layer (`graphics.pin`) and left-align the text (`graphics.alignTextLeft`) so the box grows with the name; test the longest name. 2. Keep it about 5–10 % in from the frame edges (`graphics.alignFrame.left`, then nudge in). 3. Export it as a Motion Graphics Template with the name and role editable; apply with `graphics.template.apply`.

q: Fast single-camera vlog edit: where do I start?
a: 1. Strip the pauses and filler words from the transcript (`transcript.removePauses`, `transcript.removeFillers`). 2. Keep the picture changing: punch in to about 115 % on every other cut, B-roll on V2, a lower third now and then, without zooming constantly. 3. For music sections, tap markers on the beats (M while playing) and cut to them with Snap on.

q: Run a client review round without losing the previous version.
a: 1. Duplicate the sequence before making changes (`edit.duplicate`) and date the versions. 2. Send a review export with the timecode overlay on at a modest bitrate. 3. Collect the notes as markers with comments on the sequence, and decisions in the project notes (`project.setNotes`).

q: Final checks on the mix before I export a film.
a: 1. While mixing, keep peaks around −6 dBFS and lower faders rather than limiting; a red Mix meter means the export clips. 2. Add the limiter on the Mix at the end (Hard Limiter, −1 dB). 3. Listen once on a phone or laptop speaker, not only headphones.

q: Get a thumbnail and publish the video.
a: 1. Pick a still moment (no motion blur), pause so the original is shown, and Export Frame (`file.exportFrame`) as PNG, 16-bit if you'll retouch it. 2. Watch the export once on a phone with sound on and off before publishing.

q: Start the next episode of my weekly show.
a: 1. Create it with New Project from Template (made earlier with Save as Template… on an emptied episode). 2. Keep it in one folder with Footage, Audio, Music, Graphics, Exports and Project. 3. Copy the cards with the verified copy (`card.offload`) into Footage.

q: Cut a 6.2K shoot on a slow laptop.
a: 1. Offload the cards with the verified copy (`card.offload`). 2. Let the automatic proxies build; in Auto mode playback uses the proxy and the paused frame is the original, so judge focus when stopped. 3. Watch everything once and mark selects (markers, Make Subclip) before cutting.

q: An outdoor interview has wind and the background drops out at every cut. Fix both.
a: 1. Wind: Reduce Rumble at 4 plus Voice Isolation at 10; gusts that distorted the microphone can't be repaired. 2. Gaps: lay room tone on its own track typed Ambience under the dialogue gaps, with short audio crossfades at the edits.

q: Make a tutorial from a screen recording, with chapters.
a: 1. Make a sequence at the recording's own size and frame rate (`file.newSequenceFromClip`); zoom with Motion ▸ Scale keyframes, eased. 2. Add a named marker at each chapter start (`markers.addChapter`), Export Markers as CSV (`markers.exportCsv`) and paste the times into the description, starting at 0:00; chapters under ten seconds are ignored. 3. Export at constant quality so the text stays sharp.

q: Picture lock to colour: hand the edit to someone grading elsewhere.
a: 1. Lock the picture first: no timing changes after this, so the grade isn't redone. 2. Export FCPXML or OTIO for colour (`file.exportFcpxml`) and include a reference export to check against.

q: Interviewee backlit by a window and the voice is boomy: one pass for both.
a: 1. Picture: a soft tracked ellipse window on the face, Gamma up a little, a highlight shoulder for the background; soften the window edge so there's no halo. 2. Sound: high-pass the voice around 70–100 Hz (Reduce Rumble 3–4), not above about 150 Hz or a deep voice thins.

q: End credits plus a channel logo that changes in one place.
a: 1. Credits: a paragraph text layer with Roll (`graphics.setRoll`) starting and ending off screen; the clip length sets the speed, so give it enough to read. 2. Logo: Upgrade to Source Graphic (`graphics.upgradeToSourceGraphic`) so every use updates together.
